Series::geometric_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::geometric_() const
Series& Series::geometric_(double p) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with an independent count from a geometric distribution: the number of Bernoulli trials, each with success probability p, up to and including the first success. The no-argument form uses p = 0.5.

Every sample is a positive integer: 1 means success on the first trial, 2 means one failure then a success, and so on — support starts at 1, not 0 (this convention counts the successful trial). The expected count is 1 / p, so small p gives a long right tail and a large mean.

The receiver holds the counts as its own dtype (which must be floating-point), so a Float64 buffer stores mathematically-integral values like 3.0. Internally each sample is floor(ln(1 - U) / ln(1 - p)) + 1 for a uniform U — a transformed uniform_ fill.

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the counts; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

p (double, default 0.5): the per-trial success probability. Must be strictly in (0, 1) — both endpoints are rejected (p = 0 never succeeds; p = 1 is the degenerate “always 1” case the contract excludes).

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the counts. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is not floating-point

  • if p is not strictly between 0 and 1

Gradient¶

Not differentiable — no derivative with respect to p, and the overwrite discards the receiver’s previous contents.

Examples¶

Example 1. Default p = 0.5 — positive integer counts. Seeded, so fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({10}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.geometric_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[10], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=10, contiguous=true)
data=[3.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 2.0000, 2.0000, 2.0000, 3.0000, 5.0000, 1.0000]

With p = 0.5 about half the draws are 1; the 5.0 is the tail showing up.

Example 2. Over a large sample the mean approaches 1 / p, and the minimum is 1.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.geometric_(0.25);
auto v = x.to_vec<double>();
double lo = 1e300, sum = 0;
for (double e : v) { lo = std::min(lo, e); sum += e; }
std::cout << "min=" << lo << "  mean~" << sum / v.size() << "  (1 / 0.25 = 4)\n";

Output¶

min=1  mean~3.99705  (1 / 0.25 = 4)

Example 3. The receiver must be floating-point, and p must be strictly inside (0, 1).

try {
  auto i = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
  i.geometric_(0.5);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.geometric_(0.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.geometric_(1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

geometric_: receiver must have a floating-point dtype
geometric_: expected 0 < p < 1
geometric_: expected 0 < p < 1

Example 4. Reproducible under a fixed seed.

pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.geometric_(0.4);
pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({6}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); b.geometric_(0.4);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "a == b: " << a.equal(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Support starts at 1 (the trial-count convention), not 0.

  • p must be strictly in (0, 1) — 0 and 1 both raise.

  • Floating-point receiver only; the counts are stored as integral floating values (3.0, not 3). An Int64 buffer is rejected — draw into a Float64 and to(Int64) if you want integer storage.

  • Counts are unbounded above; a small p produces a heavy right tail.

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

geometric_(p = 0.5) fills the receiver in place with trials-until-first- success counts:

  • positive integers (support starts at 1); mean 1 / p

  • p strictly in (0, 1); floating-point receiver only

  • built by inverse-CDF from a uniform draw

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • Series::bernoulli_: a single trial per element — the building block geometric_ counts.

  • Series::exponential_: the continuous analogue — waiting time rather than a discrete trial count.

  • Series::uniform_: the uniform fill geometric_ transforms internally.
